ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=\angle C$, $D$ is a point on side $BC$, and $E$ is a point on side $AC$, with $\angle ADE=\angle AED$. If $\angle BAD=28^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle ADC$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABD$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADC = \angle B + \angle BAD = \angle B + 28^\circ$, \\
and since $\angle AED$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle CDE$, \\
we have $\angle AED = \angle C + \angle EDC$, \\
considering $\angle B = \angle C$ and $\angle ADE = \angle AED$, \\
thus $\angle C + \angle EDC = \angle ADC - \angle EDC = \angle B + 28^\circ - \angle EDC$, \\
leading to the solution $\angle EDC = \boxed{14^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B and C are at the left and right ends of the base; D is located on the base BC, E is located on side AC; AD and DE are connected in the figure. It can be seen from the figure that DB and DC are opposite rays on the same straight line, AE and CE are opposite rays on the same straight line, and ray DE divides angle ADC into angle ADE and angle CDE. Reasoning: Let x=∠CDE. Looking at triangle ABD, DC is the extension direction of DB, so ∠ADC is an exterior angle of △ABD, therefore ∠ADC=∠B+∠BAD=∠B+28°. Because DE divides ∠ADC, ∠ADE=∠ADC−x=∠B+28°−x. Looking again at triangle CDE, AE is the extension direction of CE, so ∠AED is an exterior angle of △CDE, therefore ∠AED=∠C+x. It is known that ∠ADE=∠AED and ∠B=∠C, so ∠B+28°−x=∠B+x, solving gives 28°=2x, so x=14°. Therefore ∠CDE=14°.
